clue.text: Separate from icy mass, save large bears sleeping in here?

indicators.note: Here 'save' is the old preposition meaning except, so whatever it introduces is left out of the word rather than added to it.

blocks.note: a glacier calves when a chunk breaks away from it and floats off
L is the standard abbreviation for large, and it is the letter dropped here

explanation.walkthrough: Melting ice is the picture the surface sells. The question mark flags a definition by description rather than a synonym: it names where a hibernating bear spends the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: bears sleeping in here? -> CAVE: description rather than synonym, since bears hibernate in caves and the phrase points at the place instead of naming it.

clue.text: Pickle from the south-west reportedly concerning

indicators.note: What is reported comes to you by ear, so you write down a spelling that matches the sound instead of the words themselves.

blocks.note: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, so something from there is Cornish, and the sound is spelled with a CH here
a book on birds is a book concerning them

explanation.walkthrough: The word is French, which is why the spelling refuses to follow the sound, and the surface reads as a grumble about a pickle rather than a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle -> CORNICHON: the small tart gherkin served with pate and cold meats, so it names one particular pickle rather than the general word.

clue.text: Goddess given usual offers

indicators.note: To offer something is to hold it out where it can be taken, and these two words hold out a run of letters between them.

blocks.note: the run starts inside the first word and finishes inside the second, with nothing skipped in between

explanation.walkthrough: Read as English it is a sentence about generosity, which is what makes the letters easy to walk past: they never move at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Goddess -> VENUS: definition by example, since the Roman goddess of love is one goddess among many and only the crossing letters pin her down.

clue.text: Strand building that might have been shelled?

blocks.note: a strand is a beach, and the swap to the stuff that covers it is the setter's own looseness
a castle is one kind of building, a general word pointing at a particular one

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the wordplay hide inside a single noun phrase, and the question-marked half is the definition: shelled means decorated with shells and also bombarded, which is what happens to a real castle.
explanation.definitionFit: that might have been shelled? -> SANDCASTLE: children finish one with seashells pushed into the sides, and the same word means bombarded, which the surface is playing on.

clue.text: Beer drinking can lead to group feeling excited

indicators.note: A drinker takes what they drink inside them, so the beer named here holds the next letters in its middle instead of standing beside them.
The lead of a word is the letter out in front, so only the opening character of the word that follows is taken.

blocks.note: ale is beer, and this is the word that opens up to take the rest inside
a can is a tin, the thing a tin-opener opens
the opening letter of the word group

explanation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'can lead to' as one phrase about consequences. The can is a noun, and only the two words after it are the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: feeling excited -> ATINGLE: to be atingle is to prickle with anticipation, the physical symptom of excitement rather than the emotion named plainly.

clue.text: Make tracks from record inspired by Rush

indicators.note: To inspire is literally to breathe in, so the piece named before these words is drawn inside the word that follows them.

blocks.note: to dart is to rush, and this word is prised open after its first letter
an EP is an extended-play record, longer than a single and shorter than an album

explanation.walkthrough: Rush is capitalised so it reads as the rock band, and 'tracks' and 'record' keep that picture going. All three words are doing something plainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Make tracks -> DEPART: 'make tracks' is the informal phrase for leaving in a hurry, and the answer is its flat, formal equivalent.

clue.text: Trip to Cairo in February's beginning wild holiday romance?

indicators.note: Something wild is under nobody's control, and letters out of control will not stay in the order they were handed to you.
The beginning of a word is the single letter it starts with, so only the front of the month is taken into the mix.

blocks.note: thirteen letters of fodder, taken exactly as they stand
the month's opening letter makes the fourteenth

explanation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'holiday romance' as a fling. It is the genre of paperback you buy on the way to the gate, and the question mark covers the jump.
explanation.definitionFit: holiday romance? -> AIRPORT FICTION: the light novel bought at the departure gate for a fortnight away, so the phrase names a kind of book, not a fling.

clue.text: Transport for pair (sea otter and wife) swimming together

indicators.note: An otter in the water keeps to no line at all, and 'together' says the two sets of letters mix rather than stay in their own lanes.

blocks.note: eight of the nine letters to be shuffled
W is the standard abbreviation for wife, as on a family tree

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes the animal and the spouse look like an aside about a wildlife pond. They are the whole of the fodder, and 'pair' in the definition is a count of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport for pair -> TWOSEATER: a car or small aircraft built with exactly two seats, so the vehicle is named by how many people it carries.

clue.text: Scottish beast I released turns up in German city

indicators.note: Something released is let go of, so the letter named beside this word leaves the word it was sitting in.
This is a down entry, so a word that turns up is read from the bottom square to the top, back to front.

blocks.note: the monster said to live in Loch Ness is Nessie, Scotland's most famous animal
the letter I is the one let go, leaving five to be turned round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish beast' wants to be a stag. The city is in the Ruhr, Germany's old coal and steel heartland, and it is short and vowel-heavy enough that setters come back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: German city -> ESSEN: definition by example, one German city among many, so the wordplay rather than the definition is what settles which.

clue.text: Unrecognisable figures try Guinness I brewed with me

indicators.note: Stout is brewed, and brewing stirs everything named beside it about until nothing is where it started.

blocks.note: twelve letters of fodder, the stout included
the setter writes themselves in for the last two

explanation.walkthrough: In British political shorthand the men in grey suits are the anonymous party grandees who arrive quietly to tell a leader their time is up.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrecognisable figures -> MEN IN GREY SUITS: the phrase names powerful people nobody could pick out of a crowd, which is precisely what makes them unrecognisable.

clue.text: Variety published conclusion to damning exposé on the front

indicators.note: A word's conclusion is the letter it finishes on, so only the last character of the word after this is used.
The front of a word is where it starts, so this takes the opening letter of the word standing beside it.

blocks.note: a paper ran a story, which is how it published it
the closing letter of damning
the opening letter of the word, accent and all

explanation.walkthrough: The first word is italicised so it reads as the showbiz trade paper running the story. The definition is the plain noun underneath the italics.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety -> RANGE: both mean the spread of different things on offer, as in a wide range of cheeses, rather than the mountain or the cooker.

clue.text: Queen stops reprobate assuming command

indicators.note: To stop a gap is to plug it, so the letters named before this word are wedged into the middle of the ones after it.

blocks.note: an impious person has no reverence for anything, which is the reprobate the surface wants
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the crossword's standing abbreviation for a queen

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a monarch blocking a scoundrel's promotion, so 'stops' reads as halting someone. In cryptic use it is what a plug does in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: assuming command -> IMPERIOUS: an imperious person behaves as though they are in charge whether or not they are, all orders and no asking.

clue.text: Gets to dump women's footballer making you cross?

indicators.note: Dumping is throwing away, so the letter named next to these words is discarded instead of being written down.

blocks.note: one word for gets is WINS, which turns up here a letter short
W is the standard abbreviation for women, as on a lavatory door, and it is the letter thrown out
a winger plays wide on the flank, the player who delivers balls into the box

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a manager dropping a player. 'Cross' is the football noun rather than the mood, and the possessive apostrophe is hiding a single letter of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: cross? -> INSWINGER: in football an inswinger is a corner or cross that curls in towards goal, so it is one particular kind of cross.

clue.text: Cinema shortened Christmas party after reflection

indicators.note: A shortened word is one letter down, so the final character of the word beside this comes off before anything else happens.
A reflection shows a thing the other way round, so the letters assembled here are read from the far end back.

blocks.note: Christmas is NOEL, arriving here without its last letter
a do is a party or function in British usage

explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is the best-known cinema chain in Britain, and the word is also Greek for a small theatre — a name that is both a brand and a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema -> ODEON: definition by example wearing a synonym's clothes, since the chain's name is used for its buildings and an odeon is a theatre in its own right.

clue.text: Brave people hiding perhaps? I'm gonna do it!

indicators.note: Someone hiding is tucked out of sight inside something, so the letters named next sit within the word before them.

blocks.note: brave people are heroes, and the word is prised open in the middle
eg is the Latin abbreviation for 'for example', the crossword's usual reading of perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: The trap is taking 'perhaps' as the setter hedging about the bravery. It is fodder, and everything after the question mark is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: I'm gonna do it! -> HERE GOES: both are things a person says aloud at the moment of trying something risky, so the definition quotes rather than describes.

clue.text: Child protagonist hurt twice without a choice

indicators.note: 'Without a' names the letter that leaves, and 'twice' says it leaves both of the words in front of it, not just the nearer one.

blocks.note: Lee Child writes the Jack Reacher thrillers, and the hero's name turns up here minus a letter
to hurt is to ACHE, and the same letter is taken off again

explanation.walkthrough: Child is a thriller writer's surname, not a young person, which is the whole joke. The answer is French, worn into English for anything studiedly rare.
explanation.definitionFit: choice -> RECHERCHE: as an adjective 'choice' means select and out of the ordinary, and the French word means literally sought out, so both praise rarity.

clue.text: Mend circumstances broken by tension

indicators.note: A thing broken by a force is split at the point the force got in, so the letter named after this sits inside the word before it.

blocks.note: sitch is informal shorthand for the situation, the circumstances you find yourself in
T is the physicist's symbol for the tension in a rope or a string

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plot summary, circumstances broken by tension. Both content words are doing other jobs, one slang and one out of a physics textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Mend -> STITCH: to stitch a tear is to mend it with needle and thread, one specific repair standing in for the general verb.

clue.text: Unfortunately hard copy admits large and small secret

indicators.note: A door that admits someone lets them in, so the letter named after this goes inside the word standing before it.

blocks.note: H is the grade stamped on a hard pencil
to ape someone is to copy them, and this word opens up before its last letter
L is the standard abbreviation for large, the size on a clothing label
S is the standard abbreviation for small, the size below medium
sly behaviour is secret and underhand

explanation.walkthrough: Five pieces for nine letters, which is why the surface has to work so hard: 'hard copy' and 'large and small' both read as ordinary phrases and neither is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfortunately -> HAPLESSLY: hap is the old word for luck, so to do something haplessly is to do it luckless, with the misfortune attached to the doer.

clue.text: Nothing keeps American away from cake piece

indicators.note: To keep something is to hold on to it, so the word before this closes around the letters that come next.
These words name what is taken out, so the letter beside them leaves the word that follows.

blocks.note: nil is nothing in a scoreline, and it opens after its first two letters
A is the standard abbreviation for American, and it is the letter taken out
the word CAKE with the letter above removed from it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has someone guarding a cake. 'Piece' is the old word for a coin — a fifty-pence piece — and the coin here is the United States five-cent one.
explanation.definitionFit: piece -> NICKEL: 'piece' is the standard word for a coin of a stated value, and this is what Americans call their five-cent one.

clue.text: Fall over ending in you getting large bandage

indicators.note: 'Ending' takes the final letter of the word that follows, and 'in' drops that letter inside the word already built.

blocks.note: to trip is to fall over, and this word splits open after its first letter
the last letter of the word you
big is large, and it follows the single letter into the split

explanation.walkthrough: The answer looks like a brand name because it is one: the elasticated tube sold in British chemists to hold a sprained joint together.
explanation.definitionFit: bandage -> TUBIGRIP: a trade name used generically in Britain for the stretchy tube you pull over a swollen knee or ankle instead of winding a bandage round it.

clue.text: Drawing naked friends, topless men can be seen going here

definitions.text: men can be seen going here

indicators.note: A word stripped naked has lost the letters at each end, the way clothes come off the outside first, leaving the middle bare.

blocks.note: drawing here means luring, attracting someone in, and the first and last letters come off
friends are PALS, and the letter at the top drops away

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a life-drawing class and the definition is the last five words, where 'going' carries the polite sense rather than the travelling one.

clue.text: Go over hill lapping Tesla?

indicators.note: To lap something is to wrap right around it, so the word before this closes over the letters that come after.

blocks.note: a rise is a hill, a swell in the ground, and it opens after its first letter
a Tesla is an EV, an electric vehicle, and the question mark flags one make standing for the whole class

clue.text: Broadcast decorated band releases

indicators.note: A broadcast is heard rather than read, so what follows is to be taken by ear and written down some other way.

blocks.note: a frieze is the carved band running along the top of a classical wall

clue.text: 50% of ACME parts cartoon hunter cut were about to explode?

indicators.note: Fifty per cent of a word is half its letters, and the half kept here is the back one.

A word that has been cut has lost its end, so the final letter of the name in front of this comes off.

blocks.note: Elmer Fudd is the shotgun-toting hunter of the Bugs Bunny cartoons, and one D is cut away
the back half of the word, and Acme is the mail-order firm that supplies every gadget in those cartoons

clue.text: Being sixteen, suspect taking coke not OK

indicators.note: Something suspect is not to be trusted, and letters you cannot trust will not stay in the order they were given.
'Not' marks what is missing, so the two letters named after it are struck out of the word before it.

COKE loses the two letters named right after it
the pair of letters struck out of the fizzy drink above

clue.text: Cherish new wallet when penniless?

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
a wallet is a PURSE, which arrives here short of the coin letter

clue.text: Fragrant root repellent when peeled slowly at first

the opening letter of slowly

explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant root -> ORRIS: the dried rootstock of a few species of iris, kept for its violet-like scent, so the definition says exactly what the thing is.

clue.text: Designer's clothing succeeded in 8 countries, ultimately eastern style

the German city solved at 8 down, written out in full and then opened up

the last letter of countries

clue.text: Bank very heartless

indicators.note: A heartless word has had its middle removed, and in a six-letter word that means the two characters at the centre.

blocks.note: very is REALLY, and the pair of letters at its centre are gone

explanation.definitionFit: Bank -> RELY: to bank on someone is to rely on them, the same verb of trust, and each takes the same little preposition after it.
